#4260. The Top 10 Best Horror Games To Play This Halloween

Humans are drawn to horror in all forms, real life and fiction. Perhaps it’s the desire to get as close to death as possible without actually dying; perhaps it’s the morality of life and knowing death comes for all of us; perhaps all our heads are just a little miswired. Whatever the reason, we flock to movies where supernatural entities and puppets on tricycles upend otherwise lovely lives, TV shows where murderous cults kill and stump local detectives, and books where the words on the page seem to follow you to bed. Games, however, go a step further, letting you enter the horror and control it (or become its victim), and you could argue that, as a result, they’re the most immersive form of fiction.

We at Game Informer love a healthy dose of horror from time to time, and we often review games like this. Some terrify us. Others… don’t. And the best ones stick with us for years and years after the credits. Below is a list of 10 of the best horror games we’ve played recently. This isn’t an all-time list, so don’t fret if your personal favorite isn’t here. Instead, this is a collection of 10 horror games ordered by release date that we think are great for spooky season and beyond. Let us know in the comments what you would add to the list!

The cozy corner of the horror genre seems to have exploded overnight, and now tons of new slice-of-life horror games are in various stages of development. That said, the team behind newcomer The Village in the Shade is no stranger to the form; they made the Yomawari series, a cute-and-terrifying collection of creepy virtual tales. The Village in the Shade takes things back to the homestead, giving you (a child who emerged from a hole in the ground and was immediately given the responsibility of running an entire farm by yourself) the freedom to plant, sow, reap, ranch, and more. Just follow the important rules: don't go out at night, don't share secrets, and don't leave the village among others. You wouldn't want to break the rules, right? You could, theoretically, go about your idyllic rural living. But as you unravel the threads of what this village is, who you are, and why you're here, it's hard not to get drawn into the strange, mysterious, delightfully disturbing truths hiding in its shadows. Just don't forget to water your turnips before you go sneaking out again.

Fans of survival horror and old-school FMV adventure games will find plenty to love (and fear) in Tenebris Somnia. When a young woman visits her ex-boyfriend’s apartment and discovers he's trapped in a hellish dream world, it kicks off a well-executed survival-horror trek of inventive puzzles and resource management to overcome dangerous monsters. High-production, live-action cutscenes help tell the story of a deteriorating relationship and the toll an indie horror film took on its creators, and they play an important role in gameplay. Tenebris Somnia may not look like much due to its classic pixelated presentation, but its scares and story captivate. – Our Review

Resident Evil Requiem is not just one of the best Resident Evil games, but it’s also one of the best horror games ever made. It features a unique dual-protagonist structure. Grace Ashcroft is timid, new to the whole “shooting zombies in the head while dealing with Umbrella viruses” thing, and is generally just trying to do her job. Leon S. Kennedy, however, is a veteran of all that and more. Requiem splits its runtime between the two characters, letting you experience both sides of Capcom’s marquee survival-horror style. Grace’s sections leave your hands clammy and your blood pressure high as you desperately try to survive. Leon’s sections leave your hands shaking with adrenaline and your blood pumping with excitement as he mows down zombies (sometimes literally, courtesy of those pesky chainsaws). The result is a Resident Evil game that blends two typical RE experiences – terrifying and tough or exhilarating over-the-top action – into one cohesive package. It’s perfect for someone who wants to feel scared and then soon after receive the catharsis of being the one in control, like being the tragic victim who dies in Act One of the horror movie and the last one standing who lives to tell the tale. – Our Review

Little Nightmares developer Tarsier Studios has a knack for delivering creepy side-scrolling adventures, but Reanimal eschews any whimsy to become its scariest game yet. While mechanically it is similar to Little Nightmares and still puts small children in unimaginable peril, Reanimal is capital-H horror thanks largely to its terrifying threats and disturbing animal-themed imagery (this probably isn’t the game for animal lovers; some messed-up stuff happens to these critters). Escaping the game’s island setting is thrilling and chilling whether you’re playing alone or with a friend in co-op. Months after release, we’re still thinking about Reanimal’s memorable final sequence, which is worth the price of admission on its own. – Our Review

2001’s Silent Hill 2 is considered one of the best horror video games of all time for good reason. At release, it was a graphical powerhouse, using the PlayStation 2's horsepower to create a setting that begged to be explored, even though every bone in your body said you shouldn’t. The remake from developer Bloober Team took on a big task in modernizing the game without losing the original’s soul, and it did a great job. Among all the recent Silent Hill releases (Silent Hill f, Silent Hill: Townfall), the remake is our favorite. The story of James Sunderland and his troubling relationship with his departed wife is complex, emotional, and – important for the purposes of this list – unsettling and scary. – Our Review

Alan Wake 2 is an excellent pick for some spooky madness, in the vein of David Lynch’s seminal Twin Peaks mystery-surrealist series. Don’t worry too much about the “2” part of the game’s title. You just need to know that the titular Alan Wake character is a not-great writer who acts like he’s really great, his wife is missing, and he got trapped in the ambiguous Dark Place. He’s only one half of the Alan Wake 2 equation, with his segments set in a dream-like version of New York City. Playing as him feels the most Twin Peaks-y. The other half is Saga, a police officer who arrives in the Pacific Northwest town of Bright Falls to investigate a murder that might be linked to a cult. You can expect more traditional survival-horror gameplay from her. But this is still a Remedy Entertainment game, and without spoiling anything, it goes places. And along the way, you can expect plenty of scares. Turn the lights down low (or off), light a candle, and sit back and enjoy one of Remedy’s best games. – Our Review

Square Enix has gone two-for-two with its Paranormasight series, an anthology of stories about the strange and occult. And while the more recent Mermaid's Curse is a brilliant tale all its own, the first entry – The Seven Mysteries of Honjo – brings significantly more scares. A group of people in the city of Honjo find themselves caught in a spectral battle royale, using powerful objects and conditions to curse one another, with the allure of a prize at the end. Its magic isn't just in the flowchart timeline, where you can hop between different perspectives and protagonists to see how events play out from every angle, but also in the gorgeous stereoscopic environments and narrative puzzles. Adventure games are a classic genre, and Paranormasight will remind you of what the genre is capable of the moment you slowly spin your camera around, your eyes peeking out from behind your fingers.

Survival horror can contain multitudes, and as the years have worn on, the genre has grown to encompass a wide range of action-combat mechanics. Signalis feels like a re-centering in that respect. It's an isometric survival-horror indie project from developer rose-engine, filled with clever puzzles, scarce resources, limited inventory slots, and looming, oppressive dread. As the Replika unit Elster, you delve deep into a remote complex filled with horrors and monsters, searching for something, or someone, waiting down below. While love for classic horror games and other hallmarks of genre fiction will certainly draw you in, the stylish presentation and devastatingly human core will keep you forging ahead to the finale. Once you've breached the surface of Signalis' retro-future super-structures, you won't be able to turn back.

In horror movies, audiences often groan at a protagonist for putting themselves in seemingly grave danger just to learn more about a cursed amulet or bloodthirsty killer. But in Immortality, you are the protagonist, and despite a lingering sense that you shouldn't be digging into the archives of these abandoned films, each eerie new scene makes you want to dive deeper. It's a game about Marisa Marcel, an actress who almost starred in three movies in the late 20th century, but has since disappeared. None of the movies were ever released due to mysterious circumstances, but you have access to the archived, unedited live-action footage, including behind-the-scenes conversations. By scrubbing through footage, you can select people or items in each scene and jump to random footage from any other movie that includes the same person or item. The approach to puzzle-solving is unique and keeps you appropriately disoriented. The mystery at the center is an unsettling treat to unravel, and scary in new and unexpected ways. Immortality is one of a kind and an easy recommendation for horror fans who want to try something a little different.

In the decade since launch, Dead by Daylight has continued to succeed, thanks to a dedicated (and newcomer-friendly) fanbase and its towering roster of original and licensed personas from across pop culture horror. The asymmetrical multiplayer title has become an anthology of horror’s biggest faces, including Freddy Krueger, Ghostface, Pyramid Head, and even the Xenomorph. Whether you play as a Survivor, trying to escape all manner of nightmare locations through stealth and cunning, or as a Killer, whose experience feels more like a hunting club, you’ll understand why Dead by Daylight has become a recurring destination for fans of the gruesome and bizarre.

Read about the making of Dead by Daylight and how it sunk its teeth into millions of players in our six-page exclusive feature in Issue 368 (p. 42), available in our magazine archive to anyone with a free Game Informer account.

#4259. 10 Best Strategy Games Still Stuck on Older Systems

Shane is a Contributor for DualShockers writing guides and other materials. He has a degree in Game Design and Criticism.

In the world of strategy games, it can be really difficult to find one that you like that really fits what you’re looking for. Unfortunately, even when you do find a great strategy game, there’s always the chance that it won’t ever be upgraded or receive a good sequel.

It’s always a bit of a tossup for most any game that’s released on older consoles, except Skyrim and GTA V which seemingly never stop being rereleased. Some games aren’t as fortunate, despite how good they might be.

This list is a collection of some of the best strategy games that got left behind over the years. Whether it’s turn-based or real time strategy, each and every one of these games fits the bill and most definitely deserves to be brought back from the dead.

Many games based around mechs end up running into issues concerning the depth and skill required to play. Thankfully for Front Mission 4, the developers managed to figure out how to raise the game to a new level.

Front Mission 4 is actually a prequel game set before the events of Front Mission 2, bringing to life the story of two characters from the past. Players take control of the mechs piloted by our protagonists as they attempt to uncover what happened during an attack on some military bases.

The turn-based nature of the game combined with some interesting and fun mechanics makes Front Mission 4 a great candidate for a remake. The game was received generally favorably, although it was a bit sluggish in the narrative department.

Would any list of classic games be complete without the obligatory obscure JRPG? We certainly don’t think so, which is why Stella Deus: The Gate of Eternity is here. This strange JRPG feels almost like a precursor to Triangle Strategy with how it's set up.

While similar to other JRPGs in the sense of controlling a party with various classes and abilities, the game also dove heavily into the political side of things. Playing as Spero, players must navigate the difficult political issues while trying to stop the Miasma from destroying the world.

The game had interesting stakes along with a solid story exploring some harsher topics than most. This let it land fairly well amongst critics, though the lacking AI and outstanding difficulty of the game drew some ire.

Back in ye olden days of gaming, there was a glorious time where the PlayStation Portable had some truly incredible games. One of these was the tactical war game, Field Commander, which made some definitive waves when it was released.

Much like many war games, players could choose a faction and a commander which had an impact on the army’s skills and weaknesses. This led to some more than interesting choices between the factions and how each one played.

Clearly some people really enjoyed it, as it won IGN’s award for Best PSP Strategy Game of 2006. It had some excellent ideas, and might still fare well in today's landscape given the chance.

Some of your favorite companies made strategy games once upon a time. Here are 8 little-known strategy games from famous developers.

As the fourth entry into the Rebelstar series, created by Julian Gollop the creator of X-COM, it sought to upgrade the previous games in the series while making the experience more accessible to many people. With some hardcore tactical gameplay and great game design, it landed fairly well.

A truly old school plot about aliens taking over the world and a resistance rising up to fight them off ensued, and we made some truly disturbing discoveries along the way. Picking up enemy weapons and using everything the battlefield gives you were key parts of this turn-based game.

Praised highly for its combat mechanics, the game was enjoyed, although it did have issues with a lackluster story and lack of support features. Still the game made quite the impact and having that combat in the modern game generation would be nice.

Many games will attempt to make some major changes to their gameplay in an effort to reach a different set of players, and Age of Empires: Mythologies was one such game. It moved from an RTS style game to a purely turn-based one taking after the game before it.

It still worked relatively the same as previous titles, with turn-based choices resulting in battles and collecting resources. The big draw was being able to choose a particular mythology and use units, abilities, and technologies from that mythology to conquer your enemies.

While Age of Mythologies was remade for the new generation, this game was sadly left behind. It definitely brings something new to the table, especially for fans of Age of Mythology who may not really enjoy the RTS aspects, and it's a shame it hasn't been revisited.

It may sound similar to Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings, but this game is definitely different and only released for the Nintendo DS. This spin-off title changed up the RTS game and made it into a turn-based title, in an effort to make it easier to play on the handheld device.

Playing as one of the five civilizations available, players would get a hero unit along with a more defined set of units based on their civilization. Aside from combat, players could upgrade their civilizations into a new age, giving them access to more units and different technologies.

It shares many qualities with games like Civilization, though the hero aspect makes it a bit unique and would make for a good addition to the turn-based genre in this day and age. It was a solid game with great mechanics, and there was something to be said for its smaller number of civilizations and lack of online play.

Nintendo has been gradually adding new games to the Nintendo Switch Online service, but many GBA JRPGs are still stuck on the system.

There are a good number of alternate history war games, but Ring of Red was well ahead of its time. The game sought to combine turn-based and RTS mechanics to create a truly unique gameplay experience.

In a post-WWII world where Japan is split in half, what is effectively a civil war breaks out. Players would set up their units and move them in a turn-based fashion, before switching to a real time combat system.

The mechanics and design of the game made for a unique experience, especially given the mixed gameplay elements. While simple, the game offers some deeper elements, making it a fantastic strategy game by all accounts.

Most everyone at some point played an Advance Wars game if they had a DS. These are some of the best strategy titles on Nintendo handhelds. One of the very best ones was Advance Wars: Days of Ruin, thanks to some well-chosen upgrades to the systems in place.

A much darker and heavier story with some difficult threads and topics to cover, the game was set during a post-apocalyptic war. Players used Commanding Officers with special abilities to turn the tide of battle, while using various units to wipe out the enemy.

With the new units and mechanics, the game was fairly different from past entries, and praised heavily for that change. Though the story was much darker and many critics found that a bit perturbing due to the past nature of the games, it was a bold change rarely made to Nintendo-published series.

These classic games will require some work to play again, or simply an older gen console.

While perhaps not the first god game, Black & White did manage to get critical acclaim thanks to a variety of reasons. The game was made by Fable creator Peter Molyneux, and clearly infuses his unique game design and world building experience into the genre.

Players act as a god attempting to lead their people to victory over another rival god, by using their people to perform various acts. The game even has a morality system for players to use, to help them determine how their people feel about them and how they’re doing as a god.

Black & White was received incredibly well, and was both nominated for and won several awards. There’s no denying that seeing a game like this for the modern generation would be something amazing. There's something very special about this early effort.

While Advance Wars: Dual Strike may not be the first Advance Wars game in the series, it is arguably the most loved. This interesting take on the turn-based genre really put the Advance Wars series on the map for the mechanics it introduced.

Much like the rest of the series, players could use COs to control the battlefield while they attempted to wipe out the enemy units with their own. The biggest difference was the introduction of a Dual Front system, in which two separate battles occurred on each of the screens of the DS. Touchscreen control also worked very well and practically, without feeling shoehorned in.

By all accounts, the game was a raging succes,s with many calling it a significant improvement over the past titles. Though the game didn’t offer too much beyond the single new mechanic, it's still praised as one of the greatest turn-based strategy games ever made.

A list of ten games that have contributed something to the strategy genre without getting due credit.

#4256. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 30, 2026

Welcome to Devil's Night, the night before Halloween, where video games are best served scary. After tomorrow night – Halloween proper – no more scary video games allowed. At least not until mid-September, 2027. I'm sorry, I don't make the rules. Below you will find our weekend gaming recommendations (which is actually surprisingly light on scary games – apologies), but before that, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch. Beijing-based developer S-Game uses China’s Wuxia brand of action (which was actually banned for some time during the 20th Century by the country’s government) to create a stylish, fluid, and hyper-engaging combat system. It will constantly leave you in awe that action combat can look this good. But looks aren’t everything. Fortunately, Phantom Blade Zero delivers on all fronts, with weapon mechanics so detailed that picking up a new blade can feel like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. The story won’t blow your socks off, but it’s certainly engaging and enticing enough to bring you through Phantom Blade Zero’s 40 or so hours of content. If you’re not interested in the “perfect ending,” which is the only satisfactory one in my opinion, you can complete the game in less than 30 hours. S-Game mixes high-octane combat with sprawling and rewarding exploration to create a must-play during this already busy season of games. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Phantom Blade Zero review, and if you are hopping in this weekend, be sure to check out my list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks I wish I knew before starting it.

If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game. It is essentially Friday the 13th with Michael Myers instead of Jason, but with a decade of lessons learned from the team’s teeth carving in other horror properties and games. You’re either Michael or a citizen; the former wants to kill you and all the NPCs in various suburban maps, while the latter must rescue as many NPCs as possible while staying alive themselves. It’s that classic cat-and-mouse formula IllFonic is the master of, but with all the style, substance, and synths of John Carpenter’s Halloween masterpiece. Plus, Halloween: The Game features IllFonic’s first crack at a single-player campaign, and while it’s largely a tutorial for playing as Michael, if you’re a Halloween mega-fan like me, it’s worth checking out if only to take part in some of the film’s most iconic kills. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Halloween: The Game review here, and if you’re hopping in this weekend, there’s a new map, additional Halloween-themed cosmetics to unlock, and more waiting for you.

Overwatch is in the midst of its Halloween event, which have always historically been pretty interesting. This year it's Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. In it, you begin by picking one of three characters in a random role. And then, as the game progresses, you choose perks that upgrade, alter, or completely change what your character can do. It can get really chaotic where by round three characters like Orisa might be three times her normal size or Torbjorn might have placed a giant turret on Mercy's making her a flying death machine. There are also Halloween skins, as well.

Tom the Postgirl is an odd little adventure that I'd recommend to fans of Untitled Goose Game. You play as Tom, a creepy girl who's tasked with delivering packages to the people of her wacky town, which is depicted with storybook-style illustrations and a color palette limited to black, white, and red. On the surface, you're delivering packages, but the game's real story is based on Tom's tendency to peep where she shouldn't, peering into townsfolks' windows to watch their odd lives. On house is full of kids who live like dogs; another has a couple with a bizarre obsession with tickling. You never know what each window might reveal, and I quickly sympathized with (and enabled) Tom's compulsion. You also have the capacity to cause quite a bit of trouble by stomping on flowers, haphazardly snipping strings and cords, or even stealing packages and using them for your own mischievous purposes. It's a pretty short experience, completable in just a few hours, making it a nice palate cleanser between the massive releases at the end of the year.

This Devolver Digital-published game has a simple but head-turning premise. You’re a profoundly angry woman who returns to her small hometown armed with nothing but a sledgehammer, which she uses to smash everything in sight. The town is also inhabited by robots possessing human consciousnesses. Swinging the hammer can either punch holes through walls or, with enough force, reduce entire buildings to rubble. But why is she doing this? Why is she so mad? A big part of Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s allure is its fascinating and well-written tale about the protagonist’s strained relationships with her sister and mother. Learning more about their lives requires you to keep smashing, but the more you learn, the more you begin to question whether smashing everything is actually a good idea.

This bizarre indie blends fun match-3 puzzle-solving with tower defense gameplay wrapped around a funny but surreal story. The match-3 gameplay involves sliding tiles to match geographic elements like castles, trees, and rivers to collect resources that feed into the tower defense portion. Depending on how the board looks when the puzzle portion ends, you send troops (sustained by the resources you collected) to attack/defend against rival castles and gather more items; board positioning determines how well this can go. The two mechanics feed into each other to create a fun loop that grows in complexity as new mechanics are introduced. Did I mention the game is also very weird? The silly tale centers on a medieval court designating you the chosen savior to rescue their lost queen (and many other tasks), and the dumb tone adds personality to a sometimes dry genre. Titanium Court charmed and impressed us when it launched on PC earlier this year, and now console and mobile players get their chance to hold court.

Sword of the Sea is a beautiful, 2025 game about surfing through the sand atop a floating sword. It recalls Journey, the emotional 2012 PlayStation game, which makes sense as it comes from the artists and developers that worked on that game, developer Giant Squid. Giant Squid also made 2016's Abzû and 2020's The Pathless. It's a talented team and Sword of the Sea maintains that reputation. And now you can play it on Switch 2. You can read my full review of the game (though this review pertains to the PlayStation 5 version) right here.

Cities: Skylines arrived on PC more than a decade ago, but is still revered as one of the greatest modern city-builders. Even now, three years after the sequel's release, Paradox continues supporting and porting the original game. A couple years after its initial release, Cities: Skylines received a strong console port, which did an admirable job of adapting the controls to gamepads, but the Switch version was always the weakest of the bunch. As of this week, Switch 2 owners can play a less compromised version, expanding the Switch's 9-tile limit to a much larger 25-tile limit, as well as better performance and textures, better control panels, and a ton of DLC and added content. And on top of that, if you own the Switch 1 version, you get a deep discount on the Switch 2 version.

While not specifically about this new Switch 2 version, you can read our original reviews of the base PC version here, and the base console version here.

Minecraft has held its dominant spot in pop culture for so long that it's easy to forget a simple fact about it: the game is awesome. This week, it's coming to Switch 2, giving potential miners another platform to explore procedurally-generated caves in. You've certainly heard of it, and you've probably played it, but I still feel it often doesn't get the flowers it deserves in high-level critical discussions about games, despite its regular cadence of major updates. The opening gameplay loop is so satisfying that for many of my peers, whether they regularly play video games or not, it's only a matter of time before they boot up a new world again. While you can never play the game for the first time again, if you haven't checked it out in a couple years, you might be surprised by the amount of new blocks, materials, and mobs they've added in recent updates. And if you've never played before, the Switch 2 launch is as good a time as any to see what all the fuss is about.

The card game incarnation of Arkham Horror remains one of the best narrative-driven and horror-themed tabletop games around, and it's an easy recommendation if you're looking for something engaging to dive into on Halloween night. Rooted in the monsters and mysteries of the Cthulhu Mythos, this living card game is built on major core sets and expansions. But unlike a TCG, each new installment has the same cards included, fueling the cooperative adventures you'll undertake together with your fellow players. Last year Arkham Horror: The Card Game did something of a soft relaunch for a chapter 2 of its narrative, and that new core set is an ideal place to jump on  play. Players each control an individual investigator as they explore arcane and weird mysteries, confront monsters, and unfold plots of cultists, ancient entities, and forbidden lore. For fans of cosmic horror storytelling, it's an easy pick.

#4255. Battlefield 6 Season 2 delayed like many of us expected, but we're getting a new update and a bonus battle pass path

Battlefield 6 has pushed back its next season by nearly a month in order to refine Season 2 content and implement more of players' feedback.

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something new in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several new customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

#4254. Capybara Go tier list - Pets, Skills and Gear ranked

Updated on November 16th, 2026 - Version: 1.9.7 (Honor Arena)

Do you want to know what the best gear is in Capybara Go? Then let me tell you all about that because today we've got a complete Capybara Go tier list where we not only discuss weapons and armor, but also everything else you can equip.

You want your Capybara hero to be strong, so having a good build is half of that particular battle already. The rest is, of course, having the right daily encounters and a little bit of luck. But we're not talking about luck today, we're talking about factual stuff that you can have a say in. About this Capybara Go tier list I have compared all the gear you can currently get in Capybara Go, as well as all the pets and skills and ranked them into a Capybara Go tier list. The best choices are right at the very top, while the ones that might not be worth your investment sit in the lower tiers.

I made this list based on my experience and on my gameplay style, so a few things might differ for you. However, as a general rule of thumb, the top 2 tiers are universally the best, regardless of where I ranked a specific item.

As you can see, there are quite a few rarities of pets sitting atop our Capybara Go tier list of pets. That's mainly because it is extremely difficult to get an Immortal pet such as Elsa (who is also a beast), so a good alternative is going for Ice Wind Fox and Little Elle.

These two are staples in most builds, and you can easily pick one of the others whenever you get them. But given these two are Legendary rarity, chances are you'll get them a lot easier.

As for the others, I personally used Snowy and Chomper as much as I could at the beginning, until I managed to summon something better. They are okay since they can grant some useful effects, and for some Epic pets, they perform really well.

Upgrading all of your pets is something you should always do since they give you bonus passives. You don't have to use them for the active skills, just for the Upgrade Effects they provide. Upgrade them all to at least +5 (for the Hero ATK).

I need to make it very clear that skills are entirely dependent on the play style, the build you want to go for, and the gear. The skills you pick should always have good synergy with your gear, which is why I mention it in the Gear tier list when discussing situational weapons.

Now there are a lot of skills, and sometimes you will not be able to pick all the best ones. With this Capybara Go skills tier list, I hope I'll give you a clearer understanding of where each skill lands, generally speaking.

In some situations, some skills might be better and some might be worse. Take this tier list as a baseline, but always adjust it to your build.

S tier - these are generally good. You can't go wrong if you pick one of these for your build, especially since they are versatile and have the Global ATK +25% buff.

A tier - these are situational items. Depending on your play style, they could be even S-tier or S+ tier, but it also depends on the rest of your gear and the skills you go for.

B tier - Decent, but you can do better. Use this gear until you get something else. Non-S gear tier list Tier Gear name S Warrior's Sword, Warrior's Blade, Frostbite Spear, Tunic A Nomad Bow, Hawkeye Bow, Silverscale Plate, Guardian's Ring, Frostwind Horn, Icy Bubble B Nomad Staff, Forest Staff, Hard Armor, Magic Ring, Vitality Stone C Giant's Hammer, Mystic Staff, Eagle Ring D Nomad Sword

This gear is also pretty good. Considering how many copies it takes to get the S-Gear, you might sometimes be better off with these. I personally think the Frostwind Horn can be a great item, especially if you go for a full frost setup.

As for the rest, the Warrior's Blade goes really well with CRIT Mastery, so if you do get them both, you will have a really solid baseline for what the rest of your skills should be.

And that's our Capybara Go tier list with all the pets, skills and gear in the game at the moment. #4253. Aurora Gaming sweep Pixel Lumina to reach Europe Qualifier 1 final after BONK disqualification

The win completes a turnaround for a side that had already been eliminated from the qualifier. Their earlier exit had come against BONK.

The fallout reached beyond the bracket. Every BONK player and registered participant was also provisionally suspended, GINX TV reported.

The disqualification forced a rework of the schedule. Riot had set Qualifier 1 for 5 to 8 November as a single-elimination, best-of-three bracket. The Pixel Lumina semi-final and the final were pushed back to make room for the rebuilt bracket. All three affected organisations agreed to the new timetable.

Pixel Lumina, a team based in Hungary, came into the match at rank 120 in the Elo power rankings. They hold a rating of 1559 and a 30-28 record across 58 rated matches. Aurora are unranked. Before this semi-final, Pixel Lumina lost to CGN Esports in the VCL EMEA Last Chance Qualifier 2026. That defeat followed wins over FOKUS and Twisted Saints Esports in the same event.

Aurora’s lineup features Boo, chiwa, Derke, B1SK and trexx. Derke joined straight after Valorant Champions 2026, where his Vitality side lost the grand final 3-1 to LOUD.

Aurora now face the winner of xXxMasterProMegaTeamxXx versus F9 EICAR. That final decides seeding for the Kickoff Qualifier Playoffs. Aurora are already listed as qualified for the playoffs through Qualifier 1, so the final is about position rather than survival.

— Aurora Valorant (@Aurora_Valorant) November 10, 2026

The wider prize is a place at VCT EMEA Kickoff 2027. Europe will supply half of the four non-partner sides heading to the event, Riot Games said, while Türkiye and MENA each send a single team. Kickoff itself will be played offline at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin with 12 teams.

The rest of the European field is still taking shape. Europe Qualifier 2 is scheduled for 12 to 15 November and is also played as single-elimination best-of-three brackets.

#4251. Ocarina of Time Remake May Have Just Broken One of Zelda’s Biggest Traditions

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

Link has faced countless monsters, found 100 Skulltulas more than once, and saved Hyrule more times than we can count. But after all these years, one of the most recognizable things about the hero has remained largely unchanged: he rarely speaks.

That might be why a tiny detail in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has caught the attention of fans, as it appears to give Link an actual spoken line.

The discovery was recently shared by The Legend of Zelda Updates on X (formerly Twitter), which posted a clip showing Link briefly speaking Japanese during a scene with Princess Zelda.

Nintendo has expanded one of the original Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most heartbreaking side stories.

And while it's certainly not a lengthy conversation or a dramatic speech, hearing the usually silent protagonist say something out loud is still a pretty big deal for the franchise. Here, take a look by yourself (and don’t forget to turn up the volume, of course):

Watch the clip shared by The Legend of Zelda Updates on X.

This moment takes place during the game's closing sequence, as Link and Zelda attempt to escape the collapsing castle. As the hero takes hold of the princess in his arms, he can be heard saying "さあ" (pronounced "Sā"), a Japanese expression that can be translated as "come on" or "let's go," depending on the context.

There's a catch, though: the line can only be heard when playing with Japanese audio! Players using other language options won't get to hear Link deliver this little piece of dialogue, making it an especially easy detail to miss – I, for instance, played it in English and Portuguese, and I can confirm that he was silent on both.

Some of the original's most charming quirks from Zelda: Ocarina of Time didn't make the journey.

This was quickly shared on gaming forums and social media, since it appears that the Ocarina of Time remake may have broken one of the franchise’s biggest traditions of having a silent protagonist! But it is also worth pointing out that this isn't exactly the first time Link has ever spoken. The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker, for example, features a brief “Come on!” from the hero when players call companions and even a “Meow” – and I don’t know about you, but for me, that’s pretty close to this time’s “let’s go” in the remake.

This moment takes place during the game's closing sequence, as Link and Zelda attempt to escape the collapsing castle. As the hero takes hold of the princess in his arms, he can be heard saying "さあ" (pronounced "Sā"), a Japanese expression that can be translated as "come on" or "let's go," depending on the context.

Still, Link has largely remained a silent protagonist throughout the series, with his thoughts and responses usually left to the player's imagination. So, interestingly, the remake has decided to tackle that idea again, and only in the Japanese dub. And it doesn't suddenly turn Link into a talkative protagonist, nor does it suggest that Nintendo is abandoning one of the series' most recognizable traditions. It's just a small surprise that fans probably weren't expecting to hear!

And honestly, I can understand why this has caught everyone's attention. After nearly four decades of adventures, hearing Link say even a couple of syllables feels strangely significant. Whether this was an intentional creative decision or simply a small addition to the Japanese performance, it's another example of how even the tiniest changes can get Zelda fans talking!

From suspicious house designs to familiar songs, fans think they've found clues.

You can fish, catch apples, and even mine for treasure, all while encountering and freeing party mates with distinct skills in the process.

#4248. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

#4247. Dungeon Hunter 6 Lieutenants tier list

Updated on November 16th, 2026 - Version: 1.3.1

Dungeon Hunter 6 is an amazing, action-packed dungeon crawler RPG. The hack-and-slash gameplay the series is known for remains at the core of Dungeon Hunter 6, but it introduces a few tweaks to appeal to the modern player without sacrificing its distinctive charm.

In your journey to save the kingdom of Valenthia, you can carry out your mission with six selectable classes: warrior, assassin, archer, mage, shaman, and the boon sister. Notably, a significant and visually stunning change comes in the form of the new Lieutenant system, allowing you to team up with various impressive creatures in battle, each possessing a different set of skills. We decided to create this Dungeon Hunter 6 Lieutenant tier list to help you pick the best option for your character, objectives, and playstyle.

To create our Dungeon Hunter 6 tier list for all the Lieutenants, we have ranked and classified them into various tiers based on their effectiveness, skills and damage output. Here’s a breakdown of the tier rankings:

With that being said, let’s jump straight into the Dungeon Hunter 6 tier list and help you pick the best lieutenants.

S-tier Lieutenants are the best of the best, offering the most significant advantages. Here are the S-tier Lieutenants you should aim to use in every team composition: Karetta

Karetta, the vice principal at Warmage Academy, is undisputably one of the finest water element Lieutenants, who falls rather neatly into the S-Tier. Even so, her appearance reflects an ostentatious and aggressive, strong-willed personality that has a certain magic to it, a frosty one that underpins remarkably overpowered skills, rounding out a perfect damage buffer and crowd controller all in one.

Karetta possesses an active ability, Eternal Ice Jail, that’s capable of temporarily freezing enemies for three seconds. Her skill set also includes Crystal Blast, which enhances critical strike chances, and, finally, her ultimate, Power of Frost, which buffs both her and her allies' Crit Chance and Crit DMG. And in a game where damage and crowd control matter, she’s an exceptional addition to your team.

Another water element standout is the enigmatic Demonic Wolf, hailing from the Bayant Mountain Range - an archetypal, proud, and aggressive creature that seeks to become the master of the Kenashi tribe. The mysterious monster of the Kankheer snow land earns its S-Tier rank with Bleed and Burst DMG abilities while his damage scales with the target's missing HP, ensuring a perfect execution. Elsewhere, his ultimate skill, Wolf Tail, not only inflicts damage but also induces a six-second bleed effect, which is incredibly handy against bosses.

The undead champion Death Knight, who is under necromantic control, is an exceptional water element Tank. Armed with the Field of Specter skill, Death Knight grants ally teams Incoming DMG reduction and Invulnerability for three seconds. His ultimate skill, Ice Wall, further reinforces his prowess by dealing damage to opponents while lowering their attack by 30% for five seconds. Death Knight serves as a great sturdy Tank, DMG debuffer and Invulnerability caster, which, without a doubt, makes him stand at the top of this list.

Delphyne, the one-of-a-kind succubus in the fiery realm, not only attains the S-Tier, but she is also available for free, gaining acclaim as one of the game's top-tier healers. With abilities like Enchanting Torture, Lash, and the ultimate Enchanting Kiss, Delphyne demonstrates remarkable healing prowess, rescuing party members teetering on the brink of defeat. Her skill set allows her to not only save the teammate with the lowest HP but also intervene effectively in the heat of battle, as she can mitigate enemy damage reduction percentages. This attribute proves particularly advantageous against tanks and damage reduction buffers.

Terrorfiend, a commanding force in the fiery ranks, claims his place on the S-Tier through his formidable DMG Boost and Execute skills. Unleashing the power within, he harnesses the basic skill, Powerful Edge, to increase his critical hit chance by 40% for eight seconds. This, coupled with his second talent, Shattering Blow, inflicts increased damage based on the enemy's missing HP, proving his brutality and strength. Additionally, his Pummeler Storm skill descends upon adversaries, reducing their tenacity by 20% for a brief but impactful five seconds.

Archmage Herbert, the esteemed headmaster of Warmage Academy, stands as the epitome of support in the fire element, earning him the prestigious S-Tier rank. His exclusivity makes development costly, but it’s the healing Herbert casts sweetly upon allies that grounds it all. A game this big and sweeping needs an anchor, and his skillset provides a critical hit chance boost, attack speed buff, and AoE healing that does quite nicely.

Winged Terror, the leader of the harpies in the nature element, secures a position in the S-Tier with her great DMG boost and healing abilities. The harpy commander restores health to allies and herself while buffing her teammate’s ATK through her Wind Blessing skill, making her a great substitute for the old man Herbert alongside being easier to develop in the long run.

Ruins Guardian, a stalwart nature element support, attains the S-Tier thanks to its steely, unparalleled DMG reduction and shield offerings. Transforming into a stone shield with his basic ability and attaching himself to the Hero, providing widely distributed shields through puncture from above, Ruins Guardian is a steadfast character that you can count on in the deadliest and most challenging situations.

Lastly, Nora, the offspring of Ashken Chief Mahasti, is an assassin-type Lieutenant. Leading the Ashken stronghold because of the existence of many tanks, the meta has traditionally been a tough territory for assassin characters. Despite that, Nora’s doing an admirable job at taking out huge targets along with the squishy ones, thanks to her specific, well-made skillset. Her ability, Dance of Assassination, inflicts deadly damage and grants a Crit Chance Buff, while her ultimate, Phantom Combo, not only deals substantial damage but also penetrates 50% of an enemy's DEF, securing her a position in our S-Tier.

Lieutenants in the A-Tier, while not as powerful as those in S, are still robust and capable of fulfilling many roles, making them suitable for various purposes. They are simply in the A-Tier because there’s always a superior replacement who can do their role better.

From here, the information will be more concise, highlighting the most crucial points for each Lieutenant:

Lieutenants in the B-Tier are not the best, but are far from the worst. They are suitable for beginners to practice with and can be added to a team when needed, providing a balance of effectiveness and versatility. Just remember you'll want to replace them eventually, so don't get too attached.

Lieutenants in the C-Tier are not the most powerful, but they are still usable based on individual gameplay preferences. They may be suitable if they align with your playstyle or if a specific element is needed.

#4244. Best Netflix games available right now - From Into the Breach to Red Dead Redemption

Netflix isn't just a place to watch movies and TV episodes - it's also a great place for gamers to discover new forms of entertainment, with a large library of games from many different developers and genres.

There are numerous hours of fun to be had on Netflix for gamers, from action to puzzle games. On the next pages, you can find a list we compiled after carefully considering all the available games and narrowing them down to give you the top 10 best Netflix games at the moment. How to find and install Netflix Games If you don't have it already, go ahead and download the Netflix app on your device. Keep in mind that you need to have an active Netflix subscription for this.

Now, let's get on with the list of best Netflix games at the moment.

If you don't know anything about the Football Manager franchise, you must be either living under a rock or you just don't like football. But if you do like football and simulation games, then this is a no-brainer.

Become a club manager and take everything under your control, from tactics and transfers to team talks, scouting, and pretty much anything else that you can imagine.

You can start your career at any club in the world, as it supports every league and has real players. As I said, this game is a must if you are looking for a football simulation experience.

Download now! Football Manager 26 Mobile

You already know about Bloons TD 6 from our previous articles, such as Bloons TD 6 tier list and best towers to carry your rounds. In this Netflix game, you benefit from hundreds of configurations and upgrades, so feel free to read all the guides we've created to help you on that journey.

Aside from that, what you need to know about this game is that it's wild. You have a tower defence type of game where things get increasingly more difficult. Towards the last levels, some players even reported crashes because of how crazy the battles turned out.

It's one of the most fun and entertaining tower defence games out there, and easily one of the best games Netflix has to offer.

Oxenfree is a story-driven adventure game with elements of mystery and suspense, sprinkled with paranormal elements.

The story follows a group of teenagers as they face the repercussions of opening a ghostly portal on an abandoned island, while out partying one night. It's also got a smart chat system that lets players have a major impact on the tale's action and conclusion.

New graphics, a remixed soundtrack, a new epilogue, mysteries, and branching story paths can all be found in Oxenfree: Netflix Edition, which was published on September 24th, 2022. If you are interested in this title, here's a link to our full review of Oxenfree, where we get into specifics.

Before Your Eyes is a game with a major focus on storytelling and beauty. The actual story is a little dark at its core, but the way it is presented is far from it.

It gives players the opportunity to immerse themselves in an individual's life, as they journey across the River Styx and into the afterlife. That is as dark as it appears, but it has its beauty.

Before Your Eyes has innovative gameplay with real-time tracking of the player's eye movements and blinking to make choices that impact the outcome of the story. It's not something we typically see in your run-of-the-mill mobile game.

Krispee Street is an adorably designed hidden object game that is exclusively accessible to Netflix members. This title draws inspiration from a well-known webcomic, and its graphics don't shy away from showing that. It's really well done.

As a player, you'll have to figure out puzzles and discover well-hidden objects, and while it might sound like a piece of cake at first, it really isn't. Oh, and it also has a certain narrative that it manages to tell between the puzzles and hidden object games. It's really good, and a nice break from the classical, realistic hidden object game we're used to.

As a kid, you've probably dreamed of defending the Earth from various calamities or invasions and being a hero in the end. Well, Into the Breach will make your childhood dream finally come true. You're the last line of defence against the overgrown bug-like aliens that can crush a building without much effort. However, humanity has advanced, and we have huge mechs and other weapons of destruction because we humans are great at finding the best way to kill each other.

Fighting is done on an 8x8 grid that's similar to chess, with turn-based combat. As terrain can shift and create huge holes in the ground, it can be tricky to avoid them while facing aliens. Therefore, careful planning is essential to win every round, no matter what the end goal is. That's the only way to turn terrain shifts to your advantage, as gravity works on your adversaries as well.

Storyteller is a hit game unlike any other. It starts off pretty slow, with just a couple of prompts, but soon enough you will find yourself in a story unlike any other. The game is available on Steam as well, which is where it was first popularised.

The best part about Storyteller is not the fact that it's sort of a build-your-own-story kind of game, but rather its unique take on it. You will be in charge of making a plot for each prompt you're given, and sometimes these plots have a twist. Literally. It's one of the best Netflix games ever released, and you shouldn't skip it.

Red Dead Redemption likely needs no introduction, though we should take a moment to appreciate how far mobile has come before we get to that. The fact that we can now carry an incredibly complex and detailed open-world shooter like this in our pockets shows the leaps in technology since the game first released way back in 2010.

If you're somehow unfamiliar, it takes place in the Wild West and follows John Marston as he hunts down the surviving members of his old gang. Why? The federal government has taken his family and won't give them back until the job is done. Yeah, it's pretty heavy stuff and is a wonderfully told story. In some ways, I'd argue, it's better than its successor, Red Dead 2. I appreciate that’s a contentious statement, of course.

But it's not all gloomy stuff. Thanks to the open-world nature of it all, there's plenty of twisted fun to be had with tying people to train tracks and waiting for the next locomotive to roll through. Or if you don’t want to act like a Looney Tunes villain, you can swagger into a saloon, find a comfortable corner, and play poker for hours instead. It’s good fun either way.

Download now! Red Dead Redemption NETFLIX

Death might not be the happiest topic in the world, but that doesn't mean it can't provide some level of catharsis when handled well. Spiritfarer takes this complex life event and somehow manages to turn it into a cosy management RPG.

You play as a ferrymaster tasked with guiding the recently passed to the afterlife. It's not a simple case of starting the engines and sailing across to the other side, though. The spirits you encounter are somewhat restless, and you'll need to care for them as they make their final voyage. That means getting to know them and their needs, which makes for an incredibly emotional final goodbye. Still, it's that bittersweet variety of sadness where you'll be pleased you took the plunge.

Aside from chatting to Spiritfarer's lovable cast, you'll also busy yourself with fishing, crafting, mining, farming, and all manner of other things. Just because your destination is a fairly morbid one, it doesn't mean that everyday tasks can fall by the wayside, you see. They're still important and in many ways key to the relaxing vibe Spiritfarer offers.

I've had fairly mixed opinions about Black Mirror ever since it jumped to Netflix. Inspired by Black Mirror mastermind Charlie Brooker's obsession with keeping a Tamagotchi alive in his youth, Thronglets is a virtual pet sim that tasks you with helping the Throng thrive. #4242. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

#4238. Battlefield 6’s first big map in months is coming to Labs soon, but I'm more excited about BF4's Golmud Railway making its way to BF6

As promised, Battlefield Labs is coming back to bring us a preview of some of Battlefield 6’s upcoming Season 2 content.

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 currently is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off new gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

For context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its issues elsewhere, and BF Studios says it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

#4237. Capcom Reveals Fanmade Robot Master for Mega Man: Dual Override

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

The most iconic characters in the Mega Man franchise, second only to ol’ Rock himself, are the Robot Masters, the powerful, highly-specialized robots built by Dr. Light, Dr. Wily, or whoever else who are programmed to wreak havoc upon the world, usually in batches of eight. Naturally, the newest upcoming entry in the mainline series, Mega Man: Dual Override, will have a new swath of Robot Masters to do battle with, several of which like Jet Man, Cook Man, and Twinkle Girl have already been revealed.

However, in addition to these new Capcom-made Robot Masters, Dual Override is slated to bring back a long-dormant tradition of the Mega Man series: fan-designed Robot Masters. Not long after the game’s initial reveal, Capcom launched a character design contest in which fans were encouraged to design their own original Robot Master and submit it for a chance to be included in the game.

Capcom showed off a new Mega Man: Dual Override demo at Tokyo Game Show this year, proving the veteran franchise has still got it.

Many months later, Capcom has officially announced the winner of this contest and revealed the fanmade Robot Master who will be joining the rest of the new Wily Numbers. Strap on your scouring pads and turn your spray nozzles to “ON,” because our latest menace is Cleanser Man.

As director Shinya Ikuta and producer Hiroyuki Minamitani announced in a video revealed during its TwitchCon 2026 panel and posted to the official Mega Man YouTube channel, Cleanser Man was selected out of around 10,000 entrants into the contest from around the world, which then had to be meticulously narrowed down to 20 proper participants, followed by just 6 finalists. These 6 finalists included Sweeper Woman, Recycle Man, Juggle Man, Valve Man, Cactus Man, and of course, Cleanser Man.

“In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” Ikuta explained.

These 6 finalists included Sweeper Woman, Recycle Man, Juggle Man, Valve Man, Cactus Man, and of course, Cleanser Man.

According to an official character summary sent by Capcom to Game Informer, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsessive love of all things sparkling and pristine who will go to absurd lengths to scrub out any perceived imperfections, even if he ends up breaking things in the process. His stage will be set in a trash processing plant that’s flooding the world with garbage so people better appreciate his dedication to cleanliness.

The Tokyo Game Show 2026 Presentation revealed new details regarding both the second protagonist and the game's core mechanics.

Cleanser Man comes to us from a Brazilian artist who goes by “miya” on their X, formerly Twitter account. Upon the reveal that their design was chosen, they posted a screencap of Cleanser Man’s official render side-by-side with their concept art, adding the caption, “The attention to detail almost made me cry. It truly means a lot.”

Not only was the character-design contest a fun way to get people hyped up for Mega Man: Dual Override, not to mention showcase some really cool character-design work, it’s also an important revival of a long-forgotten Mega Man tradition.

Following the release of the original Mega Man game and prior to the release of Mega Man 2, Capcom held a similar contest for its Japanese players to decide the designs of that game’s eight Robot Master. This contest format would be repeated for every subsequent mainline Mega Man game up to and including Mega Man 8, resulting in many of the most notoriously-difficult Robot Masters, before being discontinued from Mega Man & Bass through Mega Man 11. While there was still some fan design encouragement, it was mostly relegated to spin-off series like Battle Network and Star Force.

While it’s only for a single Robot Master rather than a full set of eight, Cleanser Man is still the first fanmade Robot Master to make it into a mainline Mega Man title since 1996, with the added accolade that he’s the first Robot Master to come from a designer in South America. It’ll truly be an honor to shove my Buster Gun in his face.

Mega Man has had a storied career, featured in many iconic games. This list breaks down the best Mega Man games out there.

The first couple of months of 2026 in the world of Arc Raiders look pretty promising, but the big guns are being held back for now.

After weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

We’re expecting a content update each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one new map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

While we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a new matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a new Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map update during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a new Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another new Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an update to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the big guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.
